data.name: Velia
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Velia was an epithet for Venus, the goddess of love. It means swift, shining one. In Christianity, Velia can be derived from the Latin name Vibia, meaning life, living.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the swift and shining love of God.

in_hebrew.name: ווליה
in_hebrew.meaning: שם נוצרי שמקורו ביוונית ופירושו בריאה או חיה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ווליה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו ביוונית. הוא נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'וֶלִיאָה' (Oὐελία), שפירושה בריאה או חיה. השם ווליה מופיע בתקופה שלפני הספירה הנוצרית והוא קשור לתרבות היוונית העתיקה. הוא משמש כהוקרה לאלהות ולבריאה.

in_greek.name: Βελία
in_greek.meaning: Χριστιανικό όνομα που σημαίνει δημιουργία ή ζώο
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Βελία είναι ένα Χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από την ελληνική γλώσσα. Η λέξη 'Βελία' (Oὐελία) σημαίνει δημιουργία ή ζώο και έχει τις ρίζες της στην αρχαία ελληνική κουλτούρα. Το όνομα Βελία χρησιμοποιήθηκε στην αρχαία Ελλάδα και συνδέεται με τη λατρεία των θεών και τη δημιουργία του κόσμου.

data.cultural_impact: Velia holds a rich cultural significance for Christians, as it can be connected to various saints named Velia who have left an indelible mark on history. One such saint is Saint Velasius of Velia, a third-century bishop and martyr who is considered the patron saint of Vegliatica, a small village in Italy. His feast day is celebrated on May 26, and he is remembered for his unwavering faith and dedication to Christianity amidst persecution. Similarly, there is Saint Velasinda, a fourth-century virgin and martyr, who is revered in multiple locations around the world, including Italy, Borneo, and Portugal. Her feast day is celebrated on January 31, and she is invoked for protection against wild animals and natural disasters.
data.spiritual_significance: Velia holds a profound spiritual significance for Christians, as it evokes images of the supreme Goddess of Love, Venus, whose epithet it shares. Venus is regarded as the embodiment of love, beauty, and fertility, and Christians can see her influence in the concept of divine love. Furthermore, the name Velia reflects the swift and shining nature of the Christian God, whose love is pure, everlasting, and unchanging. In the context of saints named Velia, their lives serve as shining examples of selfless love and devotion, inspiring those who bear this name to live in love and kindness towards others. Overall, the name Velia carries a powerful message of divine love, beauty, and inspiration, and it is a beautiful reminder of the enduring power of love in our lives.

historical_references.reference: Velia was a site of early Christian pilgrimage in Illyria, mentioned by Saint Jerome in his letters. It is believed to have been the site of a shrine dedicated to Saint Mary Theotokos (Mother of God). The area was a popular destination for pilgrims from the Eastern Roman Empire in the 4th and 5th centuries AD.

historical_references.reference: The name Velia is also associated with the ancient city of Velia in Campania, Italy, which was a significant site for Roman culture and religion. In the Early Christian period, a basilica was built on the site, which is now known as the Basilica of Santa Maria Annunziata. The name Velia persisted into the Christian era due to its associations with Roman history and culture.
